+      expect(items(total).items.map((item) => item.value)).toEqual([3, 20, 100, null]);
+      expect(items(total).items.map((item) => item.text)).toEqual(['3', '20', '100', '']);
+      expect(items(placed).items).toEqual([
+        { value: '2026-11-04', text: '11/04/2026' },
+        { value: '2026-11-05', text: '11/05/2026' },
+        { value: '2026-11-06', text: '11/06/2026' },
+        { value: null, text: '' },
+      ]);
+    });
+
+    it('writes a datetime as its day, whichever time the first row had', () => {
+      const day = [
+        { ...A, id: 'x', at: Date.UTC(2026, 10, 5, 20, 30) },
+        { ...A, id: 'y', at: Date.UTC(2026, 10, 5, 1, 0) },
+      ];
+      expect(items(at, {}, day)).toEqual({
+        items: [{ value: '2026-11-05', text: '11/05/2026' }],
+        total: 1,
+      });
+    });
+
+    it('sorts a lookup by its text, and by the sortValue of the column when it has one', () => {
+      const byText = items(status).items.map((item) => item.text);
+      expect(byText).toEqual(['Cancelled', 'Delivered', 'New', '']);
+      expect(items(status).items.map((item) => item.value)).toEqual([3, 2, 1, null]);
+      const [ordered] = resolveColumns<Order>(
+        [
+          {
+            field: 'status',
+            dataType: 'number',
+            lookup: { items: STATUSES, valueField: 'code', displayField: 'name' },
+            sortValue: (row) => row.status,
+          },
+        ],
+        OPTIONS,
+      );
+      expect(items(ordered!).items.map((item) => item.text)).toEqual([
+        'New',
+        'Delivered',
+        'Cancelled',
+        '',
+      ]);
+    });
+
+    it('writes the value of a lookup that no item has as itself', () => {
+      const unknown = [{ ...A, status: 7 }];
+      expect(items(status, {}, unknown).items).toEqual([{ value: 7, text: '7' }]);
+    });
+
+    it('lists the blank only when a row is blank, or the condition names it', () => {
+      const noBlank = rows.filter((row) => row.status !== null);
+      expect(items(status, {}, noBlank).items.map((item) => item.value)).toEqual([3, 2, 1]);
+      expect(items(status, { named: [null] }, noBlank).items.map((item) => item.value)).toEqual([
+        3,
+        2,
+        1,
+        null,
+      ]);
+    });
+
+    it('adds the values the condition names that the rows do not hold, in their place, once', () => {
+      const result = items(status, { named: [1, 99, 2, undefined] });
+      expect(result.items.map((item) => item.value)).toEqual([99, 3, 2, 1, null]);
+      expect(result.items.find((item) => item.value === 99)).toEqual({ value: 99, text: '99' });
+      const dated = items(placed, { named: ['2026-11-01'] });
+      expect(dated.items[0]).toEqual({ value: '2026-11-01', text: '11/01/2026' });
+      expect(dated.total).toBe(5);
+      // A lookup writes a named value with the text of its item.
+      const named = items(status, { named: [3] }, [A]);
+      expect(named.items).toEqual([
+        { value: 3, text: 'Cancelled' },
+        { value: 1, text: 'New' },
+      ]);
+    });
+
+    it('narrows by a search that folds the text, and counts only what it kept', () => {
+      expect(items(customer, { search: 'an' }).items.map((item) => item.value)).toEqual([
+        'An',
+        'ấn',
+      ]);
+      expect(items(customer, { search: 'AN' }).total).toBe(2);
+      expect(items(customer, { search: 'zzz' })).toEqual({ items: [], total: 0 });
+      expect(items(customer, { search: '' }).total).toBe(4);
+    });
+
+    it('cuts the list at the limit, 500 by default, and says how many there are', () => {
+      const many = Array.from({ length: 600 }, (_, index) => ({
+        ...A,
+        id: String(index),
+        total: index,
+      }));
+      const cut = items(total, {}, many);
+      expect(cut.items).toHaveLength(500);
+      expect(cut.total).toBe(600);
+      expect(cut.items[0]!.value).toBe(0);
+      expect(cut.items[499]!.value).toBe(499);
+      const small = items(total, { limit: 10 }, many);
+      expect(small.items).toHaveLength(10);
+      expect(small.total).toBe(600);
+      // A search narrows what is counted: the list says how many are left to find.
+      const narrowed = items(total, { search: '59' }, many);
+      expect(narrowed.total).toBe(16);
+      expect(narrowed.items).toHaveLength(16);
+    });
+
+    it('lists the values of the column when it has its own, in their order, with the search and the named', () => {
+      const [remote] = resolveColumns<Order>(
+        [
+          {
+            field: 'customer',
+            headerFilter: {
+              values: [
+                { value: 'z', text: 'Zed' },
+                { value: 'a', text: 'Ann' },
+                { value: null, text: '(none)' },
+              ],
+            },
+          },
+        ],
+        OPTIONS,
+      );
+      // The rows of a page are not the values of a server: they are not read.
+      const own = items(remote!, {}, rows);
+      expect(own.items).toEqual([
+        { value: 'z', text: 'Zed' },
+        { value: 'a', text: 'Ann' },
+        { value: null, text: '(none)' },
+      ]);
+      expect(own.total).toBe(3);
+      expect(items(remote!, { search: 'AN' }, rows).items).toEqual([{ value: 'a', text: 'Ann' }]);
+      expect(items(remote!, { named: ['q'] }, rows).items.map((item) => item.value)).toEqual([
+        'z',
+        'a',
+        null,
+        'q',
+      ]);
+      expect(items(remote!, { limit: 2 }, rows)).toEqual({
+        items: [
+          { value: 'z', text: 'Zed' },
+          { value: 'a', text: 'Ann' },
+        ],
+        total: 3,
+      });
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe('headerSelection', () => {
+    const all = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'];
+
+    it('is no condition when every value is checked', () => {
+      expect(headerSelection(all, all)).toBeUndefined();
+      expect(headerSelection(all, ['d', 'c', 'b', 'a'])).toBeUndefined();
+      expect(headerSelection([], [])).toBeUndefined();
+    });
+
+    it('lists the values that are checked when half or fewer are', () => {
+      expect(headerSelection(all, ['b'])).toEqual({ values: ['b'], exclude: false });
+      expect(headerSelection(all, ['c', 'a'])).toEqual({ values: ['a', 'c'], exclude: false });
+    });
+
+    it('lists the values that are not checked, with exclude, when more than half are', () => {
+      expect(headerSelection(all, ['a', 'b', 'c'])).toEqual({ values: ['d'], exclude: true });
+      expect(headerSelection(['a', 'b', 'c'], ['a', 'b'])).toEqual({
+        values: ['c'],
+        exclude: true,
+      });
+    });
+
+    it('is a condition that keeps no row when none is checked, as the user asked', () => {
+      expect(headerSelection(all, [])).toEqual({ values: [], exclude: false });
+    });
+
+    it('takes the blank as a value, and leaves out what the list does not hold', () => {
+      expect(headerSelection([1, null, 2], [null])).toEqual({ values: [null], exclude: false });
+      expect(headerSelection([1, null, 2], [1, 2])).toEqual({ values: [null], exclude: true });
+      expect(headerSelection(all, ['b', 'zzz'])).toEqual({ values: ['b'], exclude: false });
+      expect(headerSelection(all, ['zzz'])).toEqual({ values: [], exclude: false });
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe('sameFilter', () => {
+    it('holds an empty filter and one that says its defaults to be the same', () => {
+      expect(sameFilter({}, {})).toBe(true);
+      expect(sameFilter({}, { search: '', enabled: true, columns: {} })).toBe(true);
+      expect(sameFilter({ search: 'a' }, { search: 'a' })).toBe(true);
+      expect(sameFilter({ search: 'a' }, { search: 'b' })).toBe(false);
+      expect(sameFilter({ enabled: false }, {})).toBe(false);
+      expect(sameFilter({ enabled: false }, { enabled: false })).toBe(true);
+    });
+
+    it('compares the conditions of a column by value', () => {
+      const a = filterOf({ total: { operator: 'between', value: [1, 5] } });
+      const b = filterOf({ total: { operator: 'between', value: [1, 5] } });
+      expect(sameFilter(a, b)).toBe(true);
+      expect(sameFilter(a, filterOf({ total: { operator: 'between', value: [1, 6] } }))).toBe(
+        false,
+      );
+      expect(sameFilter(a, filterOf({ total: { operator: '>', value: [1, 5] } }))).toBe(false);
+      expect(sameFilter(filterOf({ a: { exclude: false } }), filterOf({ a: {} }))).toBe(true);
+      expect(sameFilter(filterOf({ a: { exclude: true } }), filterOf({ a: {} }))).toBe(false);
+    });
+
+    it('compares the values of a header filter as sets, both ways, so repeated values cannot fool it', () => {
+      const same = (a: unknown[], b: unknown[]) =>
+        sameFilter(filterOf({ s: { values: a } }), filterOf({ s: { values: b } }));
+      expect(same(['a', 'b'], ['b', 'a'])).toBe(true);
+      expect(same(['a', 'a'], ['a'])).toBe(true);
+      expect(same(['a', 'a'], ['a', 'b'])).toBe(false);
+      expect(same(['a', 'b'], ['a', 'a'])).toBe(false);
+      expect(same([], ['a'])).toBe(false);
+      expect(same([1], ['1'])).toBe(false);
+      expect(same([null], [undefined])).toBe(false);
+      expect(sameFilter(filterOf({ s: { values: [] } }), filterOf({ s: {} }))).toBe(false);
+    });
+
+    it('compares the columns by their own keys, both ways', () => {
+      const one = filterOf({ a: { value: 1 } });
+      const two = filterOf({ a: { value: 1 }, b: { value: 2 } });
+      expect(sameFilter(one, two)).toBe(false);
+      expect(sameFilter(two, one)).toBe(false);
+      expect(sameFilter(filterOf({ a: { value: 1 } }), filterOf({ b: { value: 1 } }))).toBe(false);
+      // A key every object has is not a column that the other holds.
+      expect(sameFilter(filterOf({ constructor: { value: 1 } }), filterOf({}))).toBe(false);
+      expect(sameFilter(filterOf({}), filterOf({ constructor: { value: 1 } }))).toBe(false);
+      const same = filterOf({ constructor: { value: 1 } });
+      expect(sameFilter(same, filterOf({ constructor: { value: 1 } }))).toBe(true);
+      expect(sameFilter(same, same)).toBe(true);
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe('withRowCondition', () => {
+    it('writes the operator and the value of one column and leaves the rest of the filter', () => {

+        search: 'x',

+      expect(withRowCondition(start, 'total', undefined, [null, undefined])).toBe(start);

+      const two = filterOf({
+        customer: { value: 'a' },
+        status: { values: [1] },
+      });
+      expect(withRowCondition(two, 'customer', undefined, '')).toEqual(
+        filterOf({ status: { values: [1] } }),
+      );
+    });
+
+    it('gives back the very filter when nothing changes', () => {
+      const start = filterOf({ customer: { operator: 'contains', value: 'minh' } });

+    });
+
+    it('writes a between range, and a column whose id is constructor as an own key', () => {

+      const odd = withRowCondition({}, 'constructor', '=', 5);
+      expect(Object.hasOwn(odd.columns!, 'constructor')).toBe(true);
+      expect(conditionOf(odd, 'constructor')).toEqual({ operator: '=', value: 5 });
+      expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(odd.columns)).toBe(Object.prototype);
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe('withHeaderCondition', () => {
+    it('writes the values of one column, with exclude only when it is true, and keeps the row part', () => {
+      const start = filterOf({ status: { operator: '=', value: 1 } });
+      expect(withHeaderCondition(start, 'status', [2, null], false)).toEqual(
+        filterOf({ status: { operator: '=', value: 1, values: [2, null] } }),
+      );
+      expect(withHeaderCondition(start, 'status', [3], true)).toEqual(
+        filterOf({ status: { operator: '=', value: 1, values: [3], exclude: true } }),
+      );
+    });
+
+    it('removes the part that filters nothing: no values, or exclude with no value', () => {
+      const start = filterOf({ status: { values: [1], exclude: true }, total: { value: 1 } });
+      expect(withHeaderCondition(start, 'status', undefined, false)).toEqual(

+      );
+      // None checked is a condition that keeps no row, and stays.
+      expect(withHeaderCondition({}, 'status', [], false)).toEqual(
+        filterOf({ status: { values: [] } }),
+      );
+    });
+
+    it('removes a column left with no part, and gives back the very filter when nothing changes', () => {
+      const only = filterOf({ status: { values: [1] } });
+      expect(withHeaderCondition(only, 'status', undefined, false)).toEqual({});
+      expect(withHeaderCondition(only, 'status', [1], false)).toBe(only);
+      expect(withHeaderCondition(only, 'status', [1, 1], false)).toBe(only);
+      expect(withHeaderCondition(EMPTY_FILTER, 'status', undefined, false)).toBe(EMPTY_FILTER);
+    });
+
+    it('does not change its input, and writes a copy of the values', () => {
+      const values = [1, 2];
+      const start: DataGridFilter = Object.freeze({ search: 'x' });
+      const next = withHeaderCondition(start, 'status', values, false);
+      expect(start).toEqual({ search: 'x' });
+      values.push(3);
+      expect(next.columns!.status!.values).toEqual([1, 2]);
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe('EMPTY_FILTER', () => {
+    it('is an empty filter that no one can change', () => {
+      expect(EMPTY_FILTER).toEqual({});
+      expect(Object.isFrozen(EMPTY_FILTER)).toBe(true);
+      expect(isFiltering(EMPTY_FILTER, RESOLVED)).toBe(false);
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('does not warn for any of this', () => {
+    filterRows(ROWS, RESOLVED, filterOf({ customer: { value: 'a' }, total: { value: 5 } }), read);
+    expect(warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+});

+    it('filters by a column the grid hides, and again when that column is made again', () => {
+      const pipeline = createPipeline<Order>();
+      const hidden = pipeline.run(run({ filter: qtyOver5, columns: [idColumn] }));
+      expect(hidden.rows.length).toBeLessThan(DATA.length);

+      expect(JSON.stringify(filter)).toBe(copy);
+      expect(data).toEqual(DATA);

 });

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/filter.test-d.ts b/src/components/data-grid/filter.test-d.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..3117315
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/filter.test-d.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+import { expectTypeOf, test } from 'vitest';
+import type {
+  DataGridColumn,
+  DataGridColumnFilter,
+  DataGridFilter,
+  DataGridFilterOperator,
+} from './index';
+
+interface Order {
+  id: string;
+  customer: string;
+  total: number;
+}
+
+test('the operators are the eleven of the spec, and no other', () => {
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridFilterOperator>().toEqualTypeOf<
+    | '='
+    | '<>'
+    | '<'
+    | '>'
+    | '<='
+    | '>='
+    | 'between'
+    | 'contains'
+    | 'notContains'
+    | 'startsWith'
+    | 'endsWith'
+  >();
+  const ok: DataGridColumnFilter = { operator: 'between', value: [1, 5] };
+  expectTypeOf(ok).toBeObject();
+  // @ts-expect-error `like` is no operator
+  const like: DataGridColumnFilter = { operator: 'like', value: 'a' };
+  expectTypeOf(like).toBeObject();
+});
+
+test('the filter holds only what JSON can carry: strings, booleans, arrays and plain objects', () => {
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridFilter>().toEqualTypeOf<{
+    search?: string;
+    columns?: Readonly<Record<string, DataGridColumnFilter>>;
+    enabled?: boolean;
+  }>();
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridColumnFilter>().toEqualTypeOf<{
+    operator?: DataGridFilterOperator;
+    value?: unknown;
+    values?: readonly unknown[];
+    exclude?: boolean;
+  }>();
+  // The parts a type can pin down are no function, symbol or Date.
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridFilter['search']>().toEqualTypeOf<string | undefined>();
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridFilter['enabled']>().toEqualTypeOf<boolean | undefined>();
+  expectTypeOf<DataGridColumnFilter['exclude']>().toEqualTypeOf<boolean | undefined>();
+  const ok: DataGridFilter = {
+    search: 'minh',
+    enabled: true,
+    columns: { customer: { operator: 'contains', value: 'a' }, total: { values: [1, null] } },
+  };
+  expectTypeOf(ok).toBeObject();
+  // @ts-expect-error the search is a string
+  const numberSearch: DataGridFilter = { search: 5 };
+  expectTypeOf(numberSearch).toBeObject();
+  // @ts-expect-error a column's condition is an object
+  const loose: DataGridFilter = { columns: { customer: 'a' } };
+  expectTypeOf(loose).toBeObject();
+  // @ts-expect-error `values` is a list
+  const notAList: DataGridColumnFilter = { values: 'a' };
+  expectTypeOf(notAList).toBeObject();
+});
+
+test('a column says what it filters by with booleans, operators and a list of values with text', () => {
+  const ok: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+    { field: 'customer', allowFiltering: false, allowHeaderFiltering: false, allowSearch: false },
+    { field: 'total', filterOperators: ['>', 'between'] },
+    {
+      id: 'status',
+      value: () => 1,
+      headerFilter: {
+        values: [
+          { value: 1, text: 'New' },
+          { value: null, text: '(none)' },
+        ],
+      },
+    },
+  ];
+  expectTypeOf(ok).toBeArray();
+  // @ts-expect-error allowSearch is a boolean
+  const word: DataGridColumn<Order> = { field: 'customer', allowSearch: 'no' };
+  expectTypeOf(word).toBeObject();
+  // @ts-expect-error allowFiltering is a boolean
+  const number: DataGridColumn<Order> = { field: 'customer', allowFiltering: 1 };
+  expectTypeOf(number).toBeObject();
+  // @ts-expect-error `like` is no operator
+  const operators: DataGridColumn<Order> = { field: 'customer', filterOperators: ['like'] };
+  expectTypeOf(operators).toBeObject();
+  const noText: DataGridColumn<Order> = {
+    field: 'customer',
+    // @ts-expect-error a header value has a text
+    headerFilter: { values: [{ value: 1 }] },
+  };
+  expectTypeOf(noText).toBeObject();
+});
diff --git a/src/internal/text-fold.test.ts b/src/internal/text-fold.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..daec02a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/internal/text-fold.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,187 @@
+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
+import {
+  containsFolded,
+  findMatchFolded,
+  findMatches,
+  findMatchesFolded,
+  foldText,
+  foldWithMap,
+  includesFolded,
+} from './text-fold';
+
+describe('foldText', () => {
+  it('lower cases, removes diacritics, and turns đ into d', () => {
+    expect(foldText('Đường Hà Nội')).toBe('duong ha noi');
+    expect(foldText('ĐÀ NẴNG')).toBe('da nang');
+  });
+});
+
+describe('the Greek sigma', () => {
+  it('folds the final sigma and ς to σ, the same in the whole string and in a match', () => {
+    expect(foldText('ΟΔΟΣ')).toBe('οδοσ');
+    expect(foldText('οδος')).toBe('οδοσ');
+    expect(foldText('οδοσ')).toBe('οδοσ');
+  });
+
+  it('finds ΟΔΟΣ by οδος and by οδοσ, and the range covers it', () => {
+    for (const query of ['οδος', 'οδοσ']) {
+      expect(includesFolded('ΟΔΟΣ', query)).toBe(true);
+      expect(findMatches('ΟΔΟΣ', query)).toEqual([{ start: 0, end: 4 }]);
+    }
+  });
+});
+
+describe('containsFolded', () => {
+  it('matches an empty query, and else asks the folded text to contain the folded query', () => {
+    expect(containsFolded('ha noi', '')).toBe(true);
+    expect(containsFolded('ha noi', 'noi')).toBe(true);
+    expect(containsFolded('ha noi', 'hue')).toBe(false);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('includesFolded', () => {
+  it('finds Vietnamese text with a folded query', () => {
+    expect(includesFolded('Hà Nội', 'ha noi')).toBe(true);
+    expect(includesFolded('Đà Nẵng', 'da nang')).toBe(true);
+    expect(includesFolded('Đà Nẵng', 'DA')).toBe(true);
+    expect(includesFolded('Huế', 'huê')).toBe(true);
+  });
+
+  it('folds the text and the query the same way, NFC or NFD', () => {
+    expect(includesFolded('Đường', 'duong')).toBe(true);
+    expect(includesFolded('Đường'.normalize('NFD'), 'duong')).toBe(true);
+    expect(includesFolded('duong', 'Đường'.normalize('NFD'))).toBe(true);
+  });
+
+  it('is true for an empty query and for a query of only combining marks', () => {
+    expect(includesFolded('Hà Nội', '')).toBe(true);
+    expect(includesFolded('Hà Nội', '\u0301')).toBe(true);
+    expect(includesFolded('Hà Nội', 'xyz')).toBe(false);
+    expect(includesFolded('', 'a')).toBe(false);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('findMatches', () => {
+  it('returns the matches as UTF-16 ranges of the original text', () => {
+    expect(findMatches('Hà Nội', 'ha')).toEqual([{ start: 0, end: 2 }]);
+    expect(findMatches('Thành phố Hà Nội', 'ha noi')).toEqual([{ start: 10, end: 16 }]);
+    expect(findMatches('Đà Nẵng', 'nang')).toEqual([{ start: 3, end: 7 }]);
+  });
+
+  it('returns every match of "minh" in "Minh Minh", left to right', () => {
+    expect(findMatches('Minh Minh', 'minh')).toEqual([
+      { start: 0, end: 4 },
+      { start: 5, end: 9 },
+    ]);
+    expect(findMatches('Nguyễn Minh Anh', 'MINH')).toEqual([{ start: 7, end: 11 }]);
+  });
+
+  it('finds "duong" in "Đường", precomposed and decomposed', () => {
+    expect(findMatches('Đường', 'duong')).toEqual([{ start: 0, end: 5 }]);
+    // D + U+0111 is one letter; Đ has no decomposition, the rest does: ườ is u + two marks.
+    const decomposed = 'Đường'.normalize('NFD');
+    expect(findMatches(decomposed, 'duong')).toEqual([{ start: 0, end: decomposed.length }]);
+  });
+
+  it('does not overlap: "a" in "aaa" is three matches, "aa" in "aaa" one', () => {
+    expect(findMatches('aaa', 'a')).toEqual([
+      { start: 0, end: 1 },
+      { start: 1, end: 2 },
+      { start: 2, end: 3 },
+    ]);
+    expect(findMatches('aaa', 'aa')).toEqual([{ start: 0, end: 2 }]);
+  });
+
+  it('takes the combining marks that follow the last matched character', () => {
+    expect(findMatches('Ha\u0300 Noi', 'ha')).toEqual([{ start: 0, end: 3 }]);
+    // A match that ends before a mark takes it, the next one starts after it.
+    expect(findMatches('a\u0301a', 'a')).toEqual([
+      { start: 0, end: 2 },
+      { start: 2, end: 3 },
+    ]);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps indices right when a surrogate pair precedes or sits in the text', () => {
+    expect(findMatches('😀 Hà', 'ha')).toEqual([{ start: 3, end: 5 }]);
+    expect(findMatches('😀a😀a', 'a')).toEqual([
+      { start: 2, end: 3 },
+      { start: 5, end: 6 },
+    ]);
+    expect(findMatches('a😀b', '😀')).toEqual([{ start: 1, end: 3 }]);
+  });
+
+  it('returns nothing for an empty query, a query of only marks, and no occurrence', () => {
+    expect(findMatches('Hà Nội', '')).toEqual([]);
+    expect(findMatches('Hà Nội', '\u0301')).toEqual([]);
+    expect(findMatches('Hà Nội', 'xyz')).toEqual([]);
+    expect(findMatches('', 'a')).toEqual([]);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('findMatchesFolded and findMatchFolded', () => {
+  it('give the same ranges as findMatches on a text and a query folded once', () => {
+    const text = 'Minh gặp Minh ở Đường Minh';
+    const folded = foldWithMap(text);
+    const query = foldText('MINH');
+    expect(findMatchesFolded(text, folded, query)).toEqual(findMatches(text, 'MINH'));
+    expect(findMatchesFolded(text, folded, query)).toHaveLength(3);
+  });
+
+  it('findMatchFolded is the first of them, and null when there is none', () => {
+    const text = 'Ha Ha';
+    const folded = foldWithMap(text);
+    expect(findMatchFolded(text, folded, 'ha')).toEqual({ start: 0, end: 2 });
+    expect(findMatchFolded(text, folded, 'xyz')).toBeNull();
+    expect(findMatchFolded(text, folded, '')).toBeNull();
+  });
+});
+
+describe('foldText folds a whole string and agrees with the fold of each code point', () => {
+  // `foldWithMap` folds one code point at a time, which is what a highlight maps back through.
+  const perCodePoint = (text: string) => foldWithMap(text).folded;
+
+  it('gives for every BMP code point (lone surrogates apart) what the per-code-point fold gives', () => {
+    const differing: string[] = [];
+    for (let code = 0; code <= 0xffff; code++) {
+      if (code >= 0xd800 && code <= 0xdfff) continue;
+      const ch = String.fromCharCode(code);
+      if (foldText(ch) !== perCodePoint(ch)) differing.push(code.toString(16));
+    }
+    expect(differing).toEqual([]);
+  });
+
+  it('gives the same for a sample of astral code points', () => {
+    const differing: string[] = [];
+    for (let code = 0x10000; code <= 0x10ffff; code += 97) {
+      const ch = String.fromCodePoint(code);
+      if (foldText(ch) !== perCodePoint(ch)) differing.push(code.toString(16));
+    }
+    expect(differing).toEqual([]);
+  });
+
+  const corpus = [
+    '',
+    'Nguyễn Minh Anh 123',
+    'Đường Hà Nội, ĐÀ NẴNG đ Đ',
+    'Nguyễn Minh Anh'.normalize('NFD'),
+    'Đường Hà Nội'.normalize('NFD'),
+    'ΟΔΟΣ',
+    'οδος',
+    'Σ',
+    'ΣΑΣ ΣΟΦΟΣ. ΑΣ',
+    'İstanbul ISTANBUL ıi',
+    'a\u0301\u0323 e\u0302\u0301 ạ\u0301',
+    '\u0301 lone mark',
+    '😀 Hà 😀a👨‍👩‍👧',
+    'ǅ ǆ ẞ ß ﬁ ① Å K',
+    '한국어 ﾊﾝｸﾞﾙ',
+  ];
+
+  it('gives for each string of a corpus the joined per-code-point folds, and the text foldWithMap gives', () => {
+    for (const text of corpus) {
+      const joined = [...text].map((ch) => foldText(ch)).join('');
+      expect(foldText(text), text).toBe(joined);
+      expect(foldText(text), text).toBe(perCodePoint(text));
+    }
+  });
+});
```

-/**
- * One code point in the form both sides are compared in: lower case, without diacritics, with đ/Đ as
- * d and the final sigma ς as σ. It may come out empty (a lone combining mark) or longer. Both
- * `foldText` and `foldWithMap` fold through it, one code point at a time: lowering a whole string
- * applies context rules (the Greek final sigma) that the other would not, and the two must agree on
- * every character or a match is found in one and not shown in the other.
- */
-function foldChar(ch: string): string {
-  const base = ch.normalize('NFD').replace(/\p{M}/gu, '');
-  return (base === 'đ' || base === 'Đ' ? 'd' : base.toLowerCase()).replace(/ς/g, 'σ');
-}
-
-/** Lower case, without diacritics, with đ/Đ as d: the form both sides are compared in. */
-export function foldText(text: string): string {
-  let folded = '';
-  for (const ch of text) folded += foldChar(ch);
-  return folded;
-}
-
-/** The default rule on text already folded: an empty query matches everything, else it is contained. */
-export function containsFolded(foldedText: string, foldedQuery: string): boolean {
-  return foldedQuery === '' || foldedText.includes(foldedQuery);
-}
-
-/** The default filter: true when the folded input is empty or the folded textValue contains it. */
-export function defaultFilter(
-  item: { value: string; textValue: string },
-  inputValue: string,
-): boolean {
-  return containsFolded(foldText(item.textValue), foldText(inputValue));
-}
-
-/**
- * Where the folded query first occurs in the folded text, as UTF-16 indices into the ORIGINAL text.
- */
-export function findMatch(text: string, query: string): { start: number; end: number } | null {
-  return findMatchFolded(text, foldWithMap(text), foldText(query));
-}
-
-/**
- * `findMatch` for a text and a query that are already folded (`foldWithMap`, `foldText`), so that a
- * list folds each text once and the query once, not again for every keystroke and every item.
- */
-export function findMatchFolded(
-  text: string,
-  { folded, map }: FoldedText,
-  foldedQuery: string,
-): { start: number; end: number } | null {
-  if (foldedQuery === '') return null;
-
-  const queryChars = [...foldedQuery];
-  const textChars = [...folded];
-
-  let found = -1;
-  for (let i = 0; i <= textChars.length - queryChars.length; i++) {
-    let ok = true;
-    for (let j = 0; j < queryChars.length; j++) {
-      if (textChars[i + j] !== queryChars[j]) {
-        ok = false;
-        break;
-      }
-    }
-    if (ok) {
-      found = i;
-      break;
-    }
-  }
-  if (found === -1) return null;
-
-  const codePoints = [...text];
-  const startCodePoint = map[found];
-  const lastCodePoint = map[found + queryChars.length - 1];
-  if (startCodePoint === undefined || lastCodePoint === undefined) return null;
-  const start = utf16StartOf(codePoints, startCodePoint);
-  let end = utf16StartOf(codePoints, lastCodePoint) + codePoints[lastCodePoint]!.length;
-  for (let k = lastCodePoint + 1; k < codePoints.length; k++) {
-    const ch = codePoints[k];
-    if (ch === undefined || !/\p{M}/u.test(ch)) break;
-    end += ch.length;
-  }
-  return { start, end };
-}
-
-/** The UTF-16 start index of the i-th code point in `codePoints`. */
-function utf16StartOf(codePoints: string[], codePointIndex: number): number {
-  let u16 = 0;
-  for (let i = 0; i < codePointIndex; i++) u16 += codePoints[i]!.length;
-  return u16;
-}
-
-/** A text folded, with for each folded character the index of the code point it came from. */
-export interface FoldedText {
-  folded: string;
-  map: number[];
-}
-
-/**
- * Folds `text` code point by code point (a surrogate pair stays whole), keeping for each folded
- * character the index of the original code point it came from.
- */
-export function foldWithMap(text: string): FoldedText {
-  const codePoints = [...text];
-  const map: number[] = [];
-  let folded = '';
-  for (let i = 0; i < codePoints.length; i++) {
-    const ch = codePoints[i]!;
-    const foldedCh = foldChar(ch);
-    if (foldedCh === '') continue;
-    for (const fc of [...foldedCh]) {
-      map.push(i);
-      folded += fc;
-    }
-  }
-  return { folded, map };
-}

+import { isIsoDate } from '../../../internal/date';
+import { collator } from '../../../internal/intl';
+import { isNumber, parseNumber } from '../../../internal/number';
+import { containsFolded, foldText } from '../../../internal/text-fold';
+import type { DataGridColumnFilter, DataGridFilter, DataGridFilterOperator } from '../types';
+import { isDataColumn } from './columns';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from './columns';
+import { operatorsFor } from './operators';
+import { compareKeys } from './sort';
+import type { Comparable } from './values';
+import { isBlank } from './values';
+
+export { operatorsFor };
+
+/** The filter of a grid that filters nothing. It is frozen and shared: write a new one to change it. */
+export const EMPTY_FILTER: DataGridFilter = Object.freeze({});
+
+/** How many values the header filter lists before it says there are more (spec phase 6 §6.3). */
+const DISTINCT_LIMIT = 500;
+
+/**
+ * The texts of the cells, as the cache of `createTextCache` keeps them: what the search, the filter
+ * row and the lists read, so a cell is written and folded once for every step that wants it.
+ */
+export interface TextReader<TRow> {
+  text(row: TRow, column: { id: string; text(row: TRow): string }): string;
+  folded(row: TRow, column: { id: string; text(row: TRow): string }): string;
+}
+
+const isRecord = (value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> =>
+  typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
+
+/**
+ * A number typed in a filter cell, read the way the grid's locale writes it ("1,000.5" in `en-US`,
+ * "1.000,5" in `vi-VN`); `null` for text that is no number and for no text. The one read of a typed
+ * number: the cell, the `between` editor and the engine agree on it.
+ */
+export function parseFilterNumber(text: string, locale: string): number | null {
+  const number = parseNumber(text, locale);
+  return Number.isNaN(number) ? null : number;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The condition the filter holds for a column id. `columns` is a record keyed by ids, so it is read as
+ * an own property: a column whose id is `constructor` or `toString` has no condition by inheritance.
+ */
+export function conditionOf(filter: DataGridFilter, id: string): DataGridColumnFilter | undefined {
+  const columns: unknown = filter.columns;
+  if (!isRecord(columns) || !Object.hasOwn(columns, id)) return undefined;
+  const condition = columns[id];
+  return isRecord(condition) ? condition : undefined;
+}
+
+// The condition of a column that has a filter at all: the column of boxes has none.
+function conditionOfColumn<TRow>(
+  filter: DataGridFilter,
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+): DataGridColumnFilter | undefined {
+  return isDataColumn(column) ? conditionOf(filter, column.id) : undefined;
+}
+
+// Whether `value` is `[from, to]` with at least one end that `reads` accepts.
+function hasEnd(value: unknown, reads: (end: unknown) => boolean): boolean {
+  return Array.isArray(value) && (reads(value[0]) || reads(value[1]));
+}
+
+// The operator a row condition uses: its own, or the first one the column offers.
+function operatorOf<TRow>(
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+  condition: DataGridColumnFilter,
+): DataGridFilterOperator | undefined {
+  return condition.operator ?? column.operators[0];
+}
+
+// Whether the value is one the column reads with this operator: a string for a string column, a
+// finite number for a number, an ISO day for a date and a datetime, a boolean, and for a lookup any
+// value that is not blank. `between` needs `[from, to]` with at least one end of that kind.
+function isUsable<TRow>(
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+  operator: DataGridFilterOperator,
+  value: unknown,
+): boolean {
+  if (column.choices) return !isBlank(value);
+  const between = operator === 'between';
+  switch (column.dataType) {
+    case 'string':
+      return typeof value === 'string' && value !== '';
+    case 'boolean':
+      return typeof value === 'boolean';
+    case 'number':
+      return between ? hasEnd(value, isNumber) : isNumber(value);
+    case 'date':
+    case 'datetime':
+      return between ? hasEnd(value, isIsoDate) : isIsoDate(value);
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Whether a row condition filters: the column offers its operator (the first one when it names none)
+ * and its value is one the column reads. A condition that does not is held in the state and ignored.
+ * Whether it filters does not depend on `allowFiltering`: that is about the cell.
+ */
+export function rowConditionFilters<TRow>(
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+  condition: DataGridColumnFilter | undefined,
+): boolean {
+  if (!condition) return false;
+  const operator = operatorOf(column, condition);
+  return (
+    operator !== undefined &&
+    column.operators.includes(operator) &&
+    isUsable(column, operator, condition.value)
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * Whether a header condition filters: it holds a list of values. An empty list keeps no row, as a
+ * user who cleared every box asked; `exclude` with no value keeps every row, so it filters nothing.
+ */
+export function headerConditionFilters(condition: DataGridColumnFilter | undefined): boolean {
+  if (!condition || !Array.isArray(condition.values)) return false;
+  return !(condition.exclude === true && condition.values.length === 0);
+}
+
+/** Whether the column has a condition that filters, of either part. */
+export function columnFilters<TRow>(filter: DataGridFilter, column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>): boolean {
+  const condition = conditionOfColumn(filter, column);
+  return rowConditionFilters(column, condition) || headerConditionFilters(condition);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Whether the grid is filtering: there is a search, or the conditions are enabled and some column has
+ * a condition that filters. Every part that asks "is it filtered" (the empty state, the announcement,
+ * the funnel's fill) asks this and `columnFilters`.
+ */
+export function isFiltering<TRow>(
+  filter: DataGridFilter,
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[],
+): boolean {
+  if (typeof filter.search === 'string' && filter.search.trim() !== '') return true;
+  return filter.enabled !== false && columns.some((column) => columnFilters(filter, column));
+}
+
+type RowTest<TRow> = (row: TRow) => boolean;
+
+// A comparison of the key of a row with the value, by each ordered operator.
+function ordered<T extends number | string>(
+  operator: DataGridFilterOperator,
+  value: T,
+): ((key: T) => boolean) | undefined {
+  switch (operator) {
+    case '=':
+      return (key) => key === value;
+    case '<>':
+      return (key) => key !== value;
+    case '<':
+      return (key) => key < value;
+    case '>':
+      return (key) => key > value;
+    case '<=':
+      return (key) => key <= value;
+    case '>=':
+      return (key) => key >= value;
+    default:
+      return undefined;
+  }
+}
+
+// `[from, to]` as the ends that `read` accepts, both included; an end that is not one is open.
+function range<T extends number | string>(
+  value: unknown,
+  read: (end: unknown) => end is T,
+): (key: T) => boolean {
+  const [from, to]: unknown[] = Array.isArray(value) ? value : [];
+  const low = read(from) ? from : undefined;
+  const high = read(to) ? to : undefined;
+  return (key) => (low === undefined || key >= low) && (high === undefined || key <= high);
+}
+
+// The test of a row condition, made once for a whole list: the query folded, the number and the days
+// read. A blank cell passes `<>` and `notContains` alone (spec phase 6 §6.3).
+function rowTest<TRow>(
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+  condition: DataGridColumnFilter | undefined,
+  read: TextReader<TRow>,
+): RowTest<TRow> | undefined {
+  if (!condition || !rowConditionFilters(column, condition)) return undefined;
+  const operator = operatorOf(column, condition)!;
+  const value = condition.value;
+
+  if (column.choices || column.dataType === 'boolean') {
+    return (row) => column.filterKey(row) === value;
+  }
+
+  if (column.dataType === 'string') {
+    const query = foldText(value as string);
+    switch (operator) {
+      case 'contains':
+        return (row) => read.folded(row, column).includes(query);
+      case 'notContains':
+        return (row) => !read.folded(row, column).includes(query);
+      case 'startsWith':
+        return (row) => read.folded(row, column).startsWith(query);
+      case 'endsWith':
+        return (row) => read.folded(row, column).endsWith(query);
+      case '=':
+        return (row) => read.folded(row, column) === query;
+      default:
+        return (row) => read.folded(row, column) !== query;
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (column.dataType === 'number') {
+    const test =
+      operator === 'between' ? range(value, isNumber) : ordered(operator, value as number)!;
+    return (row) => {
+      const key = column.filterKey(row);
+      return typeof key === 'number' ? test(key) : operator === '<>';
+    };
+  }
+
+  // A date and a datetime: ISO days, which compare as text.
+  const test =
+    operator === 'between' ? range(value, isIsoDate) : ordered(operator, value as string)!;
+  return (row) => {
+    const key = column.filterKey(row);
+    return typeof key === 'string' ? test(key) : operator === '<>';
+  };
+}
+
+// The test of a header condition: the key of the row is in the values (or is not, with `exclude`).
+function headerTest<TRow>(
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+  condition: DataGridColumnFilter | undefined,
+): RowTest<TRow> | undefined {
+  if (!condition || !headerConditionFilters(condition)) return undefined;
+  // `null` is the blank; a blank that came through a form of JSON that drops it is `undefined`.
+  const values = new Set<unknown>(
+    (condition.values as unknown[]).map((v) => (v === undefined ? null : v)),
+  );
+  return condition.exclude === true
+    ? (row) => !values.has(column.filterKey(row))
+    : (row) => values.has(column.filterKey(row));
+}
+
+/**
+ * Whether the row passes the row condition of its column: strings on the column's text, folded
+ * (`contains`, `notContains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `=`, `<>`); numbers on the number; dates and
+ * datetimes on their calendar day; `between` includes both ends, and an end that is blank is open;
+ * a lookup and a boolean `=` on the value. A blank cell passes `<>` and `notContains` and nothing else.
+ * A condition that does not filter (`rowConditionFilters`) passes every row.
+ */
+export function matchesRow<TRow>(
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+  row: TRow,
+  condition: DataGridColumnFilter,
+  read: TextReader<TRow>,
+): boolean {
+  return rowTest(column, condition, read)?.(row) ?? true;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Whether the row passes the header condition of its column: its filter key is in `values`, or with
+ * `exclude` is not. A condition that does not filter (`headerConditionFilters`) passes every row.
+ */
+export function matchesHeader<TRow>(
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+  row: TRow,
+  condition: DataGridColumnFilter,
+): boolean {
+  return headerTest(column, condition)?.(row) ?? true;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The rows with the query in the text of at least one of `columns`, case and diacritics aside
+ * (`foldText`). The caller gives the columns that are shown and allow searching. The query is trimmed,
+ * and with nothing to look for the very array comes back.
+ */
+export function searchRows<TRow>(
+  rows: readonly TRow[],
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[],
+  query: string,
+  read: TextReader<TRow>,
+): readonly TRow[] {
+  const folded = foldText(query.trim());
+  if (folded === '') return rows;
+  return rows.filter((row) =>
+    columns.some((column) => containsFolded(read.folded(row, column), folded)),
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * The rows that pass every condition of every column given (all the resolved ones, the hidden too),
+ * the row part and the header part of a column joined by "and". Nothing is filtered with `enabled:
+ * false`; `except` leaves the conditions of one column out, which is how the header filter lists the
+ * values of a column narrowed by the others. When no condition filters, or no row is left out, the very
+ * array comes back. The search is not a condition: `searchRows` does it.
+ */
+export function filterRows<TRow>(
+  rows: readonly TRow[],
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[],
+  filter: DataGridFilter,
+  read: TextReader<TRow>,
+  except?: string,
+): readonly TRow[] {
+  if (filter.enabled === false) return rows;
+  const tests: RowTest<TRow>[] = [];
+  for (const column of columns) {
+    if (column.id === except) continue;
+    const condition = conditionOfColumn(filter, column);
+    if (!condition) continue;
+    const onRow = rowTest(column, condition, read);
+    if (onRow) tests.push(onRow);
+    const onHeader = headerTest(column, condition);
+    if (onHeader) tests.push(onHeader);
+  }
+  if (tests.length === 0) return rows;
+  const kept = rows.filter((row) => tests.every((test) => test(row)));
+  return kept.length === rows.length ? rows : kept;
+}
+
+/** One value of the header filter's list and what is written for it; `null` is the blank. */
+export interface DistinctItem {
+  value: unknown;
+  text: string;
+}
+
+export interface DistinctOptions {
+  /** Keeps the items whose text has this text in it, case and diacritics aside. */
+  search?: string;
+  /** Values to list that the rows may not hold: the ones the column's condition names. */
+  named?: readonly unknown[];
+  /** The most items to give; 500 when left out. */
+  limit?: number;
+  /** The locale the order of the text is by, as the grid's sort has it; `'en-US'` when left out. */
+  locale?: string;
+}
+
+// What a value that no row holds is sorted by, as the column sorts its rows: a lookup by its text, a
+// day by its time, a number as a number. A column with a `sortValue` may order the rows another way;
+// a value with no row cannot follow it.
+function sortKeyOf<TRow>(column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>, key: unknown, text: string): Comparable {
+  if (column.choices) return text === '' ? null : text;
+  if (typeof key === 'number') return key;
+  if (typeof key === 'boolean') return Number(key);
+  if (isIsoDate(key)) return Date.parse(`${key}T00:00:00Z`);
+  return typeof key === 'string' ? key : null;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The values the header filter lists for a column: the column's filter keys on `rows`, each once, with
+ * the text of its first row, in the order the column sorts (its `sortKey` of that row, so a `sortValue`
+ * orders them, and a lookup is ordered by its text), and the blank last as `null` with no text of its
+ * own. A datetime is listed by its day. `named` adds the values a condition names that no row holds.
+ * `search` keeps the items that have it in their text; `total` counts those, and `items` are the
+ * first `limit` of them. A column with its own list (`headerFilter.values`, for a server grid) lists
+ * that, in its order, and reads no row.
+ */
+export function distinctValues<TRow>(
+  rows: readonly TRow[],
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+  options: DistinctOptions,
+  read: TextReader<TRow>,
+): { items: DistinctItem[]; total: number } {
+  const { search, named = [], limit = DISTINCT_LIMIT, locale = 'en-US' } = options;
+  // `null` is the blank; a blank that came through a form of JSON that drops it is `undefined`.
+  const namedKeys = named.map((value) => (value === undefined ? null : value));
+
+  let items: DistinctItem[];
+  if (column.headerValues) {
+    items = column.headerValues.map(({ value, text }) => ({ value, text }));
+    const listed = new Set(items.map((item) => item.value));
+    for (const value of namedKeys) {
+      if (listed.has(value)) continue;
+      listed.add(value);
+      items.push({ value, text: column.keyText(value) });
+    }
+  } else {
+    const found = new Map<unknown, { text: string; sortKey: Comparable }>();
+    let blank = false;
+    for (const row of rows) {
+      const key = column.filterKey(row);
+      if (key === null) {
+        blank = true;
+      } else if (!found.has(key)) {
+        // A datetime is listed by its day, so its text is the day's and not the first row's time.
+        let text = column.dataType === 'datetime' ? '' : read.text(row, column);
+        if (text === '') text = column.keyText(key);
+        found.set(key, { text, sortKey: column.sortKey(row) });
+      }
+    }
+    for (const value of namedKeys) {
+      if (value === null) blank = true;
+      else if (!found.has(value)) {
+        const text = column.keyText(value);
+        found.set(value, { text, sortKey: sortKeyOf(column, value, text) });
+      }
+    }
+    const compareText = collator(locale, { numeric: true }).compare;
+    const order = [...found].map(([value, { text, sortKey }], index) => ({
+      item: { value, text },
+      sortKey,
+      index,
+    }));
+    order.sort((a, b) => {
+      // A value with no key to sort by comes after those that have one.
+      if (a.sortKey === null || b.sortKey === null) {
+        return a.sortKey === b.sortKey ? a.index - b.index : a.sortKey === null ? 1 : -1;
+      }
+      return compareKeys(a.sortKey, b.sortKey, compareText) || a.index - b.index;
+    });
+    items = order.map(({ item }) => item);
+    // The blank is always the last, whatever the others sort by.
+    if (blank) items.push({ value: null, text: '' });
+  }
+
+  const query = search === undefined ? '' : foldText(search);
+  if (query !== '') items = items.filter((item) => containsFolded(foldText(item.text), query));
+  return { items: items.slice(0, limit), total: items.length };
+}
+
+/**
+ * The condition that the OK of the header filter stores, from the keys of every item of the list and
+ * the keys that are checked. All checked is no condition (`undefined`); more than half is `exclude`
+ * with the ones that are not checked, which is shorter to keep; else the ones that are checked.
+ * None checked is `values: []`, a condition that keeps no row, as the user asked. A checked key the
+ * list does not hold is left out; the values come in the order of the list.
+ */
+export function headerSelection(
+  all: readonly unknown[],
+  checked: readonly unknown[],
+): { values: unknown[]; exclude: boolean } | undefined {
+  const on = new Set(checked);
+  const checkedKeys = all.filter((key) => on.has(key));
+  if (checkedKeys.length === all.length) return undefined;
+  if (checkedKeys.length * 2 > all.length) {
+    return { values: all.filter((key) => !on.has(key)), exclude: true };
+  }
+  return { values: checkedKeys, exclude: false };
+}
+
+// Two values of a condition: primitives and dates by value, a list item by item (a `between` range).
+function sameValue(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
+  if (Object.is(a, b)) return true;
+  if (a instanceof Date && b instanceof Date) return a.getTime() === b.getTime();
+  if (Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b)) {
+    return a.length === b.length && a.every((item, index) => sameValue(item, b[index]));
+  }
+  return false;
+}
+
+// Two lists of values as sets, both ways: `['a', 'a']` is not `['a', 'b']`. No list is not an empty one.
+function sameSet(a: readonly unknown[] | undefined, b: readonly unknown[] | undefined): boolean {
+  if (a === undefined || b === undefined) return a === b;
+  return a.every((item) => b.includes(item)) && b.every((item) => a.includes(item));
+}
+
+function sameCondition(a: DataGridColumnFilter, b: DataGridColumnFilter): boolean {
+  return (
+    a.operator === b.operator &&
+    sameValue(a.value, b.value) &&
+    sameSet(a.values, b.values) &&
+    (a.exclude ?? false) === (b.exclude ?? false)
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * Whether two filters are the same: the search and `enabled` (their defaults being `''` and `true`),
+ * and for each column its operator, value, values as sets and `exclude`. The columns are compared by
+ * their own keys, both ways, so a column that one holds and the other lacks is a difference.
+ */
+export function sameFilter(a: DataGridFilter, b: DataGridFilter): boolean {
+  if (a === b) return true;
+  if ((a.search ?? '') !== (b.search ?? '')) return false;
+  if ((a.enabled ?? true) !== (b.enabled ?? true)) return false;
+  const left = a.columns ?? {};
+  const right = b.columns ?? {};
+  const keys = Object.keys(left);
+  if (keys.length !== Object.keys(right).length) return false;
+  return keys.every((key) => Object.hasOwn(right, key) && sameCondition(left[key]!, right[key]!));
+}
+
+// A value a row condition can hold: not blank, and for a range at least one end that is not.
+function hasValue(value: unknown): boolean {
+  return Array.isArray(value) ? value.some((end) => !isBlank(end)) : !isBlank(value);
+}
+
+// The filter with the condition of one column replaced; no part left in it removes the column, and
+// no column left removes `columns`. The very filter comes back when nothing changed.
+function withCondition(
+  filter: DataGridFilter,
+  id: string,
+  condition: DataGridColumnFilter,
+): DataGridFilter {
+  const columns = filter.columns ?? {};
+  let next: DataGridFilter;
+  if (Object.keys(condition).length > 0) {
+    next = { ...filter, columns: { ...columns, [id]: condition } };
+  } else {
+    const rest = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(columns).filter(([key]) => key !== id));
+    next = { ...filter };
+    if (Object.keys(rest).length > 0) next.columns = rest;
+    else delete next.columns;
+  }
+  return sameFilter(filter, next) ? filter : next;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The filter with the row condition of one column written: the operator the caller names, and the
+ * value when it is not blank (a range needs one end). A blank value is not stored, but an operator
+ * the user chose stays, so the cell still shows it; no operator and no value takes the row part away.
+ * The header part of the column stays, and a column left with no part is removed.
+ */
+export function withRowCondition(
+  filter: DataGridFilter,
+  id: string,
+  operator: DataGridFilterOperator | undefined,
+  value: unknown,
+): DataGridFilter {
+  const { values, exclude } = conditionOf(filter, id) ?? {};
+  const next: DataGridColumnFilter = {};
+  if (operator !== undefined) next.operator = operator;
+  if (hasValue(value)) next.value = value;
+  if (values !== undefined) next.values = values;
+  if (exclude !== undefined) next.exclude = exclude;
+  return withCondition(filter, id, next);
+}
+
+/**
+ * The filter with the header condition of one column written: `values`, and `exclude` when it is true.
+ * No values, or `exclude` with none, takes the header part away. The row part of the column stays,
+ * and a column left with no part is removed. The values are copied.
+ */
+export function withHeaderCondition(
+  filter: DataGridFilter,
+  id: string,
+  values: readonly unknown[] | undefined,
+  exclude: boolean,
+): DataGridFilter {
+  const { operator, value } = conditionOf(filter, id) ?? {};
+  const next: DataGridColumnFilter = {};
+  if (operator !== undefined) next.operator = operator;
+  if (value !== undefined) next.value = value;
+  if (values !== undefined && !(exclude && values.length === 0)) {
+    next.values = [...values];
+    if (exclude) next.exclude = true;
+  }

+import type { DataGridDataType, DataGridFilterOperator } from '../types';
+
+const TEXT: readonly DataGridFilterOperator[] = [
+  'contains',
+  'notContains',
+  'startsWith',
+  'endsWith',
+  '=',
+  '<>',
+];
+const ORDERED: readonly DataGridFilterOperator[] = ['=', '<>', '<', '>', '<=', '>=', 'between'];
+const EQUALS: readonly DataGridFilterOperator[] = ['='];
+
+/**
+ * The operators the filter row can offer a column of this type, the default first (spec phase 6 §6.3):
+ * text `contains`, numbers and days `=`, and only `=` for a boolean or a column with a lookup, which
+ * the filter row draws as a `Select`. The lists are shared and not to be changed.
+ */
+export function operatorsFor(
+  dataType: DataGridDataType,
+  hasLookup: boolean,
+): readonly DataGridFilterOperator[] {
+  if (hasLookup) return EQUALS;
+  switch (dataType) {
+    case 'string':
+      return TEXT;
+    case 'boolean':
+      return EQUALS;
+    case 'number':
+    case 'date':
+    case 'datetime':
+      return ORDERED;
+  }
+}

+/**
+ * Text folded to be compared: lower case, without diacritics, with đ/Đ as d. One rule for every
+ * place a grid or a list matches text (the Combobox filter and its bold match, the DataGrid search,
+ * filter row and header filter), with no locale: the text on the server and in the browser must
+ * fold the same way, and a Turkish `İ` or `I` would not match what the user types on another
+ * keyboard.
+ */
+
+/**
+ * One code point in the form both sides are compared in: lower case, without diacritics, with đ/Đ as
+ * d and the final sigma ς as σ. It may come out empty (a lone combining mark) or longer. Both
+ * `foldText` and `foldWithMap` fold through it, one code point at a time: lowering a whole string
+ * applies context rules (the Greek final sigma) that the other would not, and the two must agree on
+ * every character or a match is found in one and not shown in the other.
+ */
+function foldChar(ch: string): string {
+  const base = ch.normalize('NFD').replace(/\p{M}/gu, '');
+  return (base === 'đ' || base === 'Đ' ? 'd' : base.toLowerCase()).replace(/ς/g, 'σ');
+}
+
+/**
+ * Lower case, without diacritics, with đ/Đ as d: the form both sides are compared in. The whole string
+ * is folded in one pass (a search folds every cell once, and a code point at a time is five times
+ * slower); it gives the very text `foldChar` gives code point by code point, which the tests hold
+ * for every BMP code point and for a corpus (a Greek final sigma is the one context rule, and the
+ * last replace makes it σ as `foldChar` does).
+ */
+export function foldText(text: string): string {
+  return text
+    .normalize('NFD')
+    .replace(/\p{M}/gu, '')
+    .replace(/[đĐ]/g, 'd')
+    .toLowerCase()
+    .replace(/ς/g, 'σ');
+}
+
+/** The rule on text already folded: an empty query matches everything, else it is contained. */
+export function containsFolded(foldedText: string, foldedQuery: string): boolean {
+  return foldedQuery === '' || foldedText.includes(foldedQuery);
+}
+
+/** The rule on raw text: `containsFolded` of both folded. An empty query matches everything. */
+export function includesFolded(text: string, query: string): boolean {
+  return containsFolded(foldText(text), foldText(query));
+}
+
+/** A range of UTF-16 indices in a text, `end` exclusive. */
+export interface TextRange {
+  start: number;
+  end: number;
+}
+
+/** A text folded, with for each folded character the index of the code point it came from. */
+export interface FoldedText {
+  folded: string;
+  map: number[];
+}
+
+/**
+ * Folds `text` code point by code point (a surrogate pair stays whole), keeping for each folded
+ * character the index of the original code point it came from.
+ */
+export function foldWithMap(text: string): FoldedText {
+  const codePoints = [...text];
+  const map: number[] = [];
+  let folded = '';
+  for (let i = 0; i < codePoints.length; i++) {
+    const ch = codePoints[i]!;
+    const foldedCh = foldChar(ch);
+    if (foldedCh === '') continue;
+    for (const fc of [...foldedCh]) {
+      map.push(i);
+      folded += fc;
+    }
+  }
+  return { folded, map };
+}
+
+/** The UTF-16 start index of the i-th code point in `codePoints`. */
+function utf16StartOf(codePoints: string[], codePointIndex: number): number {
+  let u16 = 0;
+  for (let i = 0; i < codePointIndex; i++) u16 += codePoints[i]!.length;
+  return u16;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The occurrences of the folded query in a folded text, left to right and without overlap, as UTF-16
+ * ranges of the ORIGINAL text; at most `limit`. A range takes the combining marks that follow its
+ * last character, which the fold dropped. Empty when the query is empty.
+ */
+function scan(
+  text: string,
+  { folded, map }: FoldedText,
+  foldedQuery: string,
+  limit: number,
+): TextRange[] {
+  if (foldedQuery === '') return [];
+  const queryChars = [...foldedQuery];
+  const textChars = [...folded];
+  const codePoints = [...text];
+  const ranges: TextRange[] = [];
+
+  let i = 0;
+  while (i <= textChars.length - queryChars.length && ranges.length < limit) {
+    let ok = true;
+    for (let j = 0; j < queryChars.length; j++) {
+      if (textChars[i + j] !== queryChars[j]) {
+        ok = false;
+        break;
+      }
+    }
+    if (!ok) {
+      i++;
+      continue;
+    }
+    const startCodePoint = map[i];
+    const lastCodePoint = map[i + queryChars.length - 1];
+    if (startCodePoint === undefined || lastCodePoint === undefined) break;
+    const start = utf16StartOf(codePoints, startCodePoint);
+    let end = utf16StartOf(codePoints, lastCodePoint) + codePoints[lastCodePoint]!.length;
+    for (let k = lastCodePoint + 1; k < codePoints.length; k++) {
+      const ch = codePoints[k];
+      if (ch === undefined || !/\p{M}/u.test(ch)) break;
+      end += ch.length;
+    }
+    ranges.push({ start, end });
+    i += queryChars.length;
+  }
+  return ranges;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Where the folded query first occurs in a folded text, as UTF-16 indices into the ORIGINAL text.
+ * The text and the query are already folded (`foldWithMap`, `foldText`), so that a list folds each
+ * text once and the query once, not again for every keystroke and every item.
+ */
+export function findMatchFolded(
+  text: string,
+  folded: FoldedText,
+  foldedQuery: string,
+): TextRange | null {
+  return scan(text, folded, foldedQuery, 1)[0] ?? null;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Every occurrence of the folded query in a folded text, left to right and without overlap, as UTF-16
+ * ranges of the original text: what a search marks in a cell.
+ */
+export function findMatchesFolded(
+  text: string,
+  folded: FoldedText,
+  foldedQuery: string,
+): TextRange[] {
+  return scan(text, folded, foldedQuery, Infinity);
+}
+
+/** `findMatchesFolded` for a raw text and a raw query, which it folds. */
+export function findMatches(text: string, query: string): TextRange[] {
+  return findMatchesFolded(text, foldWithMap(text), foldText(query));
+}
```

+import { act, createEvent, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';

+import { FILTER_ANNOUNCE_DELAY } from './hooks/use-rows-found';
+import { DEFAULT_LABELS } from './labels';

+// The filter state of the grid (spec phase 6 §6.1, §6.3 "Lọc"): a controllable value like the sort, the
+// first page after a change, the rows found, `clearFilter()` and the grid that is empty because of its
+// filter. The search field and the cells of the filter row come in later tasks; until then the filter
+// is given as a prop and cleared by the handle and by the button of the empty grid.
+

+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  resetDevWarnings();
+  HTMLElement.prototype.checkVisibility = () => true;
+});
+afterEach(() => {
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'checkVisibility');
+  vi.useRealTimers();
+  vi.restoreAllMocks();
+});
+
+interface Order {
+  id: string;
+  customer: string;
+  qty: number;
+}
+
+const makeOrders = (count: number): Order[] =>
+  Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => ({
+    id: `DH-${1000 + index}`,
+    customer: `Customer ${index + 1}`,
+    qty: index + 1,
+  }));
+
+const ORDERS = makeOrders(12);
+
+const COLUMNS: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
+  { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, width: 104 },
+  { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer', width: 200 },
+  { field: 'qty', caption: 'Qty', dataType: 'number', width: 80 },
+];
+
+/** Keeps the rows whose customer holds "Customer 1": Customer 1, 10, 11 and 12. */
+const SOME: DataGridFilter = { search: 'Customer 1' };
+/** Keeps no row. */
+const NONE: DataGridFilter = { search: 'nobody at all' };
+
+function Orders({
+  gridRef,
+  ...props
+}: Partial<DataGridProps<Order>> & { gridRef?: Ref<DataGridHandle> }) {
+  return (
+    <DataGrid
+      ref={gridRef}
+      data={ORDERS}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={COLUMNS}
+      caption="Orders"
+      paging={false}
+      {...props}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+const grid = () => screen.getByRole('grid') as HTMLTableElement;
+const bodyRows = () => Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tbody > tr'));
+const dataRows = () => grid().querySelectorAll('tbody > tr.flg-data-grid-row');
+const stops = () => Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[tabindex="0"]'));
+const live = () => document.querySelector('[aria-live]')!.textContent;
+const clearButton = () => screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Clear filter' });
+const head = (caption: string) =>
+  Array.from(grid().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('thead th')).find((th) =>
+    th.textContent?.startsWith(caption),
+  )!;
+const press = (element: HTMLElement, key: string, init: KeyboardEventInit = {}): boolean => {
+  const event = createEvent.keyDown(element, { key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...init });
+  act(() => {
+    fireEvent(element, event);
+  });
+  return event.defaultPrevented;
+};
+const advance = (ms: number) => act(() => void vi.advanceTimersByTime(ms));
+
+describe('the filter state', () => {
+  it('filters the rows of an uncontrolled grid by defaultFilter, and shows it in getState()', () => {
+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();
+    render(<Orders gridRef={ref} defaultFilter={SOME} />);
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(4);
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().filter).toEqual(SOME);
+  });
+
+  it('is empty by default: no condition, nothing filtered', () => {
+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();
+    render(<Orders gridRef={ref} />);
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(12);
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().filter).toEqual({});
+  });
+
+  it('follows a controlled filter, and a change from outside calls no callback', () => {
+    const onFilterChange = vi.fn();
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn();
+    const { rerender } = render(
+      <Orders filter={{}} onFilterChange={onFilterChange} onStateChange={onStateChange} />,
+    );
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(12);
+    rerender(
+      <Orders filter={SOME} onFilterChange={onFilterChange} onStateChange={onStateChange} />,
+    );
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(4);
+    rerender(
+      <Orders filter={NONE} onFilterChange={onFilterChange} onStateChange={onStateChange} />,
+    );
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(0);
+    expect(onFilterChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    expect(onStateChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it('filters by a condition of a column, the hidden one too', () => {
+    const filter: DataGridFilter = { columns: { qty: { operator: '>', value: 10 } } };
+    render(<Orders defaultFilter={filter} defaultColumnLayout={{ hidden: ['qty'] }} />);
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(2);
+  });
+
+  it('holds a condition of a column that comes after mount, and filters when it arrives', () => {
+    const filter: DataGridFilter = { columns: { qty: { operator: '>', value: 10 } } };
+    const ref = createRef<DataGridHandle>();
+    const { rerender } = render(<Orders gridRef={ref} columns={[]} defaultFilter={filter} />);
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().filter).toEqual(filter);
+    rerender(<Orders gridRef={ref} columns={COLUMNS} defaultFilter={filter} />);
+    expect(dataRows()).toHaveLength(2);
+    expect(ref.current!.getState().filter).toEqual(filter);
+  });
+
+  it('ignores a condition of an unknown column, an operator the column lacks and a value it cannot read, with no word', () => {
+    const spy = warn();
+    const filter: DataGridFilter = {
+      columns: {
+        nobody: { operator: '=', value: 1 },
+        qty: { operator: 'contains', value: 'a' },
+        customer: { operator: 'contains', value: 5 },
+        ['constructor']: { operator: '=' as const, value: 'x' },
+      },

+      outside = setFilter;
+      return <Orders gridRef={ref} filter={filter} onFilterChange={setFilter} />;
+    }

+    for (let change = 0; change < 3; change++) {
+      act(() => ref.current!.clearFilter());

+      act(() => outside(SOME));

+  // rows that stay (a row that moves to another place is a row of another place, and draws again).
+  const SOME = { columns: { qty: { operator: '<' as const, value: 5 } } };
+  const small = (props: Partial<React.ComponentProps<typeof DataGrid<Order>>> = {}) => (
+    <DataGrid
+      data={rows}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={COLUMNS}
+      caption="Orders"
+      paging={false}
+      {...props}
+    />
+  );
+  const reset = () => {
+    renders.cell = 0;
+    renders.headerCell = 0;
+    renders.toolbar = 0;
+    renders.body = 0;
+  };
+
+  it('draws no title and no row that stays for a filter that keeps more rows, only the rows that come', () => {
+    const onFilterChange = () => {};
+    const { rerender } = render(small({ filter: SOME, onFilterChange }));
+    expect(screen.getAllByRole('row')).toHaveLength(1 + 4);
+    reset();
+    rerender(small({ filter: {}, onFilterChange }));
+    expect(screen.getAllByRole('row')).toHaveLength(1 + 12);
+    // The 8 rows that come draw their 3 cells; the 4 that stay and the 3 titles do not.
+    expect(renders.cell).toBe(8 * 3);
+    expect(renders.headerCell).toBe(0);
+  });
+
+  it('draws no cell and no title for a filter that keeps fewer rows', () => {
+    const onFilterChange = () => {};
+    const { rerender } = render(small({ filter: {}, onFilterChange }));
+    reset();
+    rerender(small({ filter: SOME, onFilterChange }));
+    expect(screen.getAllByRole('row')).toHaveLength(1 + 4);
+    expect(renders.cell).toBe(0);
+    expect(renders.headerCell).toBe(0);
+  });
+
+  it('draws no row again for a filter and a handler written inline that say what they said before', () => {
+    const { rerender } = render(
+      small({ filter: { ...SOME }, defaultFilter: { search: 'x' }, onFilterChange: () => {} }),
+    );
+    reset();
+    rerender(
+      small({ filter: { ...SOME }, defaultFilter: { search: 'x' }, onFilterChange: () => {} }),
+    );
+    expect(renders.cell).toBe(0);
+    expect(renders.headerCell).toBe(0);
+  });
+
+  it('draws no title and no row that stays when the grid is cleared', () => {
+    const ref = { current: null as import('./index').DataGridHandle | null };
+    render(small({ defaultFilter: SOME, ref } as never));
+    reset();
+    act(() => ref.current!.clearFilter());
+    expect(renders.cell).toBe(8 * 3);
+    expect(renders.headerCell).toBe(0);
+  });
+});

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/DataGridFiltering.stories.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/DataGridFiltering.stories.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..fcf0739
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/DataGridFiltering.stories.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,178 @@
+import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
+import { useState } from 'react';
+import { expect, fn, waitFor } from 'storybook/test';
+import { bodyCell, SALES, SALE_COLUMNS, noTitleIsCut } from '../../../.storybook/data-grid-orders';
+import type { Sale } from '../../../.storybook/data-grid-orders';
+import { realUserEvent } from '../../../.storybook/real-input';
+import { DataGrid } from './DataGrid';
+import type { DataGridFilter, DataGridProps } from './index';
+
+const meta = {
+  title: 'Components/DataGrid/Filtering',
+  component: DataGrid,
+  // Built but not released until the grid is exported (spec phase 6 §2): hidden from the sidebar of
+  // the built docs, still run by the story tests and shot by the visual harness.
+  tags: ['unreleased'],
+  args: { data: SALES, rowKey: 'id', columns: SALE_COLUMNS, 'aria-label': 'Orders' },
+  parameters: {
+    a11y: {
+      config: {
+        rules: [{ id: 'region', enabled: false }],
+      },
+    },
+  },
+} satisfies Meta<DataGridProps<Sale>>;
+
+export default meta;
+type Story = StoryObj<DataGridProps<Sale>>;
+
+/**
+ * How long a story waits for the grid to show what a press asked of it: the state changes in the
+ * press, and the commit and the focus it gives come in the engine's next rendering update, which Linux
+ * WebKit on x86 (CI) delivers late. `waitFor` waits one second by default; a late update came within
+ * five. Each message says what was missing, so a late update can be told from one that never came.
+ */
+const RENDER_UPDATE = { timeout: 5000 };
+
+/** A filter that keeps no order: nobody has this name. */
+const NO_ORDER: DataGridFilter = { search: 'nobody has this name' };
+
+const titleOf = (root: HTMLElement, caption: string) =>
+  Array.from(root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('thead th')).find((th) =>
+    th.textContent?.startsWith(caption),
+  )!;
+
+/** The grids of `EmptyByFilter`: one empty because of its filter, held by the story, and one with no data. */
+const EmptyGrids = ({
+  onFilterChange,
+}: {
+  onFilterChange: DataGridProps<Sale>['onFilterChange'];
+}) => {
+  const [filter, setFilter] = useState<DataGridFilter>(NO_ORDER);
+  return (
+    <div style={{ width: 760, display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
+      <DataGrid
+        aria-label="Filtered orders"
+        data={SALES}
+        rowKey="id"
+        columns={SALE_COLUMNS}
+        paging={false}
+        filter={filter}
+        onFilterChange={(next) => {
+          setFilter(next);
+          onFilterChange?.(next);
+        }}
+      />
+      <DataGrid
+        aria-label="No orders"
+        data={[]}
+        rowKey="id"
+        columns={SALE_COLUMNS}
+        paging={false}
+      />
+    </div>
+  );
+};
+
+/**
+ * A grid that is empty because of its filter (spec phase 6 §4.3 "Trống do lọc"): a ring with a funnel
+ * crossed out, the words, and the button that clears the filter, in the box a grid with no data
+ * draws its words in. The button is the one place of the body: reached by ↓ from the titles (which
+ * keeps the column), left by ↑, one Tab stop in the table, pressed by Enter, and then the rows are back
+ * and the focus is on the first cell. A grid with no data has no button.
+ */
+export const EmptyByFilter: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  args: { onFilterChange: fn() },
+  render: (args) => <EmptyGrids onFilterChange={args.onFilterChange} />,
+  play: async ({ canvasElement, args }) => {
+    const [root, plain] = Array.from(canvasElement.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid'));
+    const table = root!.querySelector<HTMLTableElement>('table[role="grid"]')!;
+    const stops = () => table.querySelectorAll('[tabindex="0"]');
+    const button = () =>
+      root!.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.flg-data-grid-empty-content button')!;
+    await noTitleIsCut(root!);
+
+    // The words and the button of the filtered grid; the other grid has its own words and no button.
+    const content = root!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-empty-content')!;
+    const plainContent = plain!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-empty-content')!;
+    await expect(content.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-empty-title')).toHaveTextContent(
+      'No rows match the filter',
+    );
+    await expect(button()).toHaveTextContent('Clear filter');
+    await expect(plainContent).toHaveTextContent('No data');
+    await expect(plain!.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-empty button')).toBeNull();
+
+    // The box is the box of the words of a grid with no data: the same padding, width, text and place.
+    const same = ['paddingTop', 'paddingRight', 'paddingBottom', 'paddingLeft', 'width'] as const;
+    const boxOf = getComputedStyle(content);
+    const plainBox = getComputedStyle(plainContent);
+    for (const property of same) await expect(boxOf[property], property).toBe(plainBox[property]);
+    for (const property of ['position', 'left', 'textAlign', 'fontSize', 'fontWeight'] as const) {
+      await expect(boxOf[property], property).toBe(plainBox[property]);
+    }
+    // Its parts: the ring is 38px with a funnel of 18px, 8px apart from the words and the button, all
+    // of them on the middle line of the box.
+    const ring = content.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-empty-icon')!;
+    await expect([ring.offsetWidth, ring.offsetHeight]).toEqual([38, 38]);
+    await expect(getComputedStyle(ring).borderRadius).toBe('50%');
+    const funnel = ring.querySelector('svg')!;
+    await expect([funnel.clientWidth, funnel.clientHeight]).toEqual([18, 18]);
+    await expect(boxOf.rowGap).toBe('8px');
+    const middle = content.getBoundingClientRect().left + content.getBoundingClientRect().width / 2;
+    for (const part of [ring, content.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-empty-title')!, button()]) {
+      const box = part.getBoundingClientRect();
+      await expect(Math.abs(box.left + box.width / 2 - middle), part.className).toBeLessThan(1.5);
+    }
+    // The only stop of the table is the button.
+    await expect(Array.from(stops())).toEqual([button()]);
+
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    // Pressed on a title, the place is the title of Customer; ↓ reaches the button, ↑ leaves it for that title.
+    const customer = titleOf(root!, 'Customer');
+    await real.click(customer);
+    await expect(customer).toHaveFocus();
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowDown}');
+    await expect(button()).toHaveFocus();
+    await expect(Array.from(stops())).toEqual([button()]);
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowUp}');
+    await expect(customer).toHaveFocus();
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowDown}');
+    await expect(button()).toHaveFocus();
+
+    // Keys that move along a row have no neighbour to go to, and nothing scrolls.
+    const page = [window.scrollX, window.scrollY];
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}{ArrowRight}{Home}{End}{ArrowDown}');
+    await expect(button()).toHaveFocus();
+    await expect([window.scrollX, window.scrollY]).toEqual(page);
+
+    // One Tab leaves the grid (it has one stop), and Shift+Tab comes back to it.
+    await real.tab();
+    await expect(
+      table.contains(document.activeElement),
+      `focus is on ${document.activeElement?.outerHTML.slice(0, 160)}`,
+    ).toBe(false);
+    await real.tab({ shift: true });
+    await expect(button()).toHaveFocus();
+
+    // Enter presses the button: one change of the filter, the rows are back, the focus is on the first cell.
+    await real.keyboard('{Enter}');
+    await expect(args.onFilterChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+    await expect(args.onFilterChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith({});
+    await waitFor(
+      () =>
+        expect(
+          table.querySelectorAll('tbody > tr.flg-data-grid-row').length,
+          'the rows are back',
+        ).toBe(SALES.length),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(bodyCell(root!, 0, 0), 'the focus is on the first cell').toHaveFocus(),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(Array.from(stops())).toEqual([bodyCell(root!, 0, 0)]);
+    await expect(root!.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-empty')).toBeNull();
+  },
+};
